newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends unchanged on weak demand.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends unchanged on weak demand.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices closed unchanged after another uneventful session marred by lack of consumer demand, traders said.

They said trading was likely to stay quiet through the holiday-shortened week. The market will be closed on Friday for the Moslem Eid al-Adha holiday. "The market could fall another two to three cents this week if buyers did not return," said one local trader.
Traders said producers have been reluctant to lower their offer prices, but rising domestic stocks due to weak demand could force them to do so.
At the close, May RSS1 buyer was quoted by the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board at 290.50 cents ($1.16) a kg, unchanged from Friday.
May SMR 20 buyer also ended unchanged at 275 cents ($1.10).
Trading houses quoted SMR CV at 343 cents a kg, SMR L at 323, SMR 10 at 276 and drum latex at 233 FOB.
The INRO five-day moving average was 222.22 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on April 11 against 222.86 on April 10. The daily indicator price was 221.03 versus 221.64.
